articles.title: Your first TildeRadio show
articles.summary: Get an account, find your controls, test your stream and know what to do before, during and after a show.
articles.keywords: first beginner handbook onboarding butt mixxx live broadcast

blocks.text: Say hello in #tilderadio and ask about a regular show, occasional set or one-off broadcast. An administrator supplies your AzuraCast DJ streaming account and enables its website access.

items.label: Sign in to the DJ booth

blocks.text: Use your personal DJ username and password. Never share them in IRC, a public profile, a screenshot or a repository.

The DJ booth is your starting point. My profile edits your public identity and recurring show. Your assigned schedules book airtime. Prepare a show saves a one-show title and optional playlist. Live / IRC runs the current broadcast. Sets / broadcasts corrects the public archive.

items.label: Understand the different kinds of show information

blocks.text: TildeRadio’s existing live connection settings are below. Use your own DJ credentials and confirm station-specific connection details with an administrator if your assignment differs.

The existing test broadcaster port is 8015. Confirm that your account has test-station access before connecting. Listen to the test station from another device or headphones to check sound, levels and metadata.

items: Book airtime in your assigned schedule. A prepared show or a planned archive listing does not reserve the slot.
Optionally prepare an episode title and an ordered song list. Link your IRC services account if you want DJ bot controls.
At your agreed airtime, connect your broadcaster. Check the public station and Live / IRC to confirm that your DJ is live.
With a prepared playlist, use Start next song or !track next when each song actually begins. Otherwise Carrier captures the stream’s metadata.
Use only the interaction you want. Automatic song announcements start off unless you opt in for this show.
Disconnect when finished. Review the captured set in Sets / broadcasts and correct missing metadata if needed.

blocks.text: Choose the intended input or application output in your broadcaster. Use your desktop’s audio routing tools to verify the path before going live.
Ask in #tilderadio with your software, operating system and exact error. Keep credentials out of messages. Website access, station assignments and streaming access are separate checks.

articles.title: Where to do what
articles.summary: A quick map of profiles, airtime bookings, preparations, live controls and archived broadcasts.
articles.keywords: navigation schedule plan listing booth profile difference timezone UTC

rows: Change my bio or recurring show name
Your public DJ page and recurring show defaults
Plan one episode and its song order
A preparation for one broadcast window
Advance songs or manage tonight’s interaction
Fix titles, times or a past track list
The recording attached to a published listing
Activate another DJ or assign a station

blocks.text: A recurring show belongs to your profile. An episode or set is one broadcast. A schedule entry reserves airtime. A preparation adds optional episode information and planned songs. A broadcast listing describes what appears in the archive. These are connected, but saving one does not create or replace the others.

The schedule editor displays the assigned station’s timezone. Show preparation and broadcast-listing editors explicitly use UTC. Your profile’s show timezone selects weekday formats; it does not change the timezone of a booking or preparation. Check the labels beside the times before saving.

sections.title: Why someone else has more buttons

blocks.text: Ordinary DJs edit their assigned profile, station schedules, preparations and broadcast listings. Live controls belong to the verified live DJ. Administrators have broader access. Reading this Help area grants no editing access. Optional Carrier/recording tools may be unavailable when the station has not enabled them.

articles.title: Sign in and get editing access
articles.summary: Use your DJ streaming account, then check website activation, your profile link and station assignments.
articles.keywords: login password authenticate azuracast credentials disabled assignment streamer id station

items: Open the DJ booth and enter your personal AzuraCast DJ streaming username and password.
If access is disabled, ask an administrator to enable the corresponding website DJ account.
If your profile is unlinked or no station appears, ask the administrator to link your public profile and assign the correct station DJ account.

sections.title: A login and an assignment are different

blocks.text: A working streaming password proves your DJ identity. Website activation controls login/editing. A profile link controls which public DJ page and broadcast listings you manage. Station assignments choose which station schedules and live streamer you can control. Changing a public name does not change those account IDs.

items: Password not accepted: check the DJ streaming credentials, not an AzuraCast administrator login.
Website access disabled: contact the station administrator.
Too many attempts: wait five minutes before retrying.
Form expired: reload the login page for a fresh form.
Temporarily unavailable: the authentication service cannot currently verify the account; retry later.

blocks.text: Use Sign out in the DJ booth when you are finished. Never send your password or a linking code to a public channel.

articles.title: Configure your streaming software
articles.summary: Enter the Icecast connection details in BUTT, Mixxx or another compatible broadcaster.
articles.keywords: butt mixxx broadcast port mount 8005 128 mp3 ogg icecast connection SSL

blocks.text: These values retain the station’s existing handbook settings. A different assigned station may use different ports. Use the account-specific connection information supplied by the administrator. Listening URLs are not broadcaster connection URLs.

items: Open Settings and add a server.
Select Icecast. Enter the host, port, mount, DJ username and DJ password.
Choose the intended audio input and a supported encoder format. The existing station handbook uses 128 kbps MP3 as a compatibility baseline.
Test on the test station first, then connect to the main stream at your agreed airtime.

blocks.text: Open Preferences → Live Broadcasting. Select Icecast 2 and enter your station connection information. Set the encoder format supported by your setup; AzuraCast’s guide also describes Ogg Vorbis. Test the connection and audio before your slot.

Keep saved broadcaster configurations private. If TLS/SSL is available, use the station’s exact TLS connection instructions. Do not guess that the DJ port accepts TLS because the website uses HTTPS. Ask the administrator when the broadcaster reports a certificate or connection error.

articles.title: Test your stream before a show
articles.summary: Check audio, routing, metadata and the connection without taking over the main station.
articles.keywords: test station 8015 8010 sound silent clipping levels

blocks.text: The existing test broadcaster port is 8015 on azuracast.tilderadio.org. Confirm test-station credentials/access with the administrator; a main-station DJ account is not a promise of test access.

items: Select the intended microphone, mixer or application audio in the broadcaster.
Play a short track and speak into the microphone if you plan to use one.
Monitor from a separate device or headphones. Allow for streaming delay.
Check that neither source clips and that the microphone/music balance is comfortable.
Change artist/title metadata and confirm the listener view updates.
Disconnect the test stream and select the main-station connection before show time.

blocks.text: Do not send your own delayed station playback back into the broadcaster. Keep monitoring separate from the audio source you transmit.

articles.title: Audio routing and microphone checks
articles.summary: Choose what the broadcaster hears and keep monitoring out of the transmitted audio.
articles.keywords: linux pipewire pulseaudio pactl pavucontrol microphone feedback loopback null sink mixer

items: Identify the music/application output and microphone you intend to transmit.
Select the intended input or mixer in your broadcaster.
Use your desktop mixer or routing tool to send only those sources to that input.
Listen through headphones or a separate device and check music/microphone levels on the test station.

blocks.text: Keep desktop notifications and station playback out of the transmitted path unless you intentionally want them on air.

sections.title: Linux with PipeWire or PulseAudio compatibility

blocks.text: Device and application names depend on your desktop. Your audio mixer can show the broadcaster’s recording input; choose the correct device or monitor. PipeWire also provides pw-link to inspect and connect ports. Use its official reference for the commands supported by your installation.

For a setup that intentionally uses PulseAudio-compatible virtual sinks, this creates a named output whose monitor can be selected in the broadcaster. Route the chosen application into it through your mixer. This is an optional advanced example, not a requirement for normal broadcasting.

pactl load-module module-null-sink sink_name=tilderadio_mix sink_properties=device.description=TildeRadio_Mix
pavucontrol

Select Monitor of TildeRadio_Mix as the broadcaster input and direct the intended application output into TildeRadio_Mix. Microphone mixing requires an additional deliberate route. Record returned module IDs so you can unload only modules you created. Do not restart your audio server or set every volume to maximum as a troubleshooting shortcut.

articles.title: Edit your profile and recurring show
articles.summary: Update your public biography, links, avatar and the show details Carrier uses as defaults.
articles.keywords: bio biography avatar genres favorites show title timezone formats weekday JSON git

items: Sign in and open My profile in the DJ booth.
Edit your public name, biography, avatar, links and any optional personal details.
Set the recurring show title, description, genres and show timezone.
Save and check your public DJ page.

blocks.text: If the page is unavailable, ask an administrator to link your account to the correct profile. A profile edit is not an account password change.

The advanced formats field accepts JSON. Each format has a lowercase ID and weekday names in days, with optional title, tagline, description and genres. Carrier resolves the format using your show timezone. Keep one-show episode titles in a preparation or Live / IRC.

Publish only information you want listeners to see. An unpublished profile is hidden from the public catalog; the administrator still manages the account separately. Never put streaming credentials in biography, links, notes or JSON.
Experienced contributors can continue using profile JSON files and the validator. The website editor is the normal DJ workflow; Git knowledge is not required.

articles.title: Book, change or cancel airtime
articles.summary: Use your assigned station schedule and understand overlap rejection and station timezones.
articles.keywords: schedule airtime slot overlap conflict timeslot timezone overnight recurring days cancel delete

items: Open the DJ booth and find Your assigned schedules.
Choose the station you want to broadcast on.
Reload its schedule and choose the dates/days and start/end times shown by the editor.
Save. The editor checks against other entries and rejects an overlapping timeslot.

sections.title: If a slot is already taken

blocks.text: The new or edited overlapping booking is rejected. Choose a free time or coordinate a handoff/change with the affected DJ and an administrator. A rejected save does not reserve the slot. If the schedule changed while the form was open, reload it before trying again.
Use the station timezone displayed in the schedule editor. Recheck day selections and dates when a show crosses midnight. This differs from the UTC times used by preparations and broadcast listings.

sections.title: Move or cancel an existing booking

blocks.text: Open your entry in the assigned station schedule. Save its revised times or use its remove control and confirmation. Ordinary DJs manage only their assigned DJ’s entries; administrators can manage station entries more broadly. Cancelling a booking does not delete a captured archive set.

sections.title: Then prepare the episode if you want

blocks.text: Preparation is optional and separate from scheduling. A saved playlist, a public preview or a planned archive listing does not book airtime.

articles.title: Prepare an episode and song list
articles.summary: Save episode details and optional song order before going live, then confirm actual playback during the show.
articles.keywords: playlist setlist song order copy plan UTC artist title tab spreadsheet immutable reminder upcoming preview

items: Book your airtime first. Open Prepare a show → Prepare a new show.
Choose your assigned station and expected start/end in UTC. The window must be at most twelve hours.
Add an episode title and any topic, mood, prompt, note or link.
Optionally enter ordered songs as Artist | Title, one per line. Two spreadsheet columns separated by a tab also work.
Choose public title/topic preview, a private linked-account reminder or song announcements only if wanted.
Save before going live and allow website synchronization to complete.

blocks.text:
Artist One | Song One
Artist Two | Song Two

Carrier uses your verified station/streamer assignment and expected time window to select one matching enabled preparation. If none or several match, it uses ordinary metadata capture. A preparation is copied once when attached; later edits to the original do not rewrite the live set.

sections.title: The list does not mark songs as played

blocks.text: Playback begins at song zero. Start song one with Start next song or !track next, then advance when the next song actually starts. Jumping to a later number timestamps only that song. Unplayed songs stay out of public playback feeds.

items.label: Advance songs and choose tracking mode

blocks.text: You can edit an unused preparation, copy one for a new broadcast, or cancel it. An attached preparation is immutable; change the live controls or its completed broadcast listing instead. A copy requires fresh times and starts with automatic song announcements off. Cancelling preparation leaves the AzuraCast booking intact.

Publishing a preview exposes the upcoming episode title/topic, not the unplayed playlist. A private reminder goes to a linked, verified IRC services account when the integration can deliver it. Neither option is required to broadcast.

articles.title: Run your live show from the website
articles.summary: Find song advances, episode details, listener queues, polls and handoff controls in one place.
articles.keywords: live IRC requests question queue poll listener goal handoff mood topic prompt

blocks.text: Sign in and open Live / IRC. Carrier must see your live stream and verify it against the assigned station DJ. Your show title, listeners, current song and tracking mode appear here.

rows: Confirm playback in a prepared playlist
Choose prepared playback or captured metadata
Enable or disable automatic song messages for this show
Episode title, topic, mood, prompt, note and link
Open requests and resolve queued listener items
Name the DJ expected to take over
One optional DJ note for the set, when configured

blocks.text: Only the verified live DJ and administrators can change the current broadcast. Wait for a radio poll/synchronization cycle after connecting, then refresh the page. If Carrier is offline or assignments cannot be verified, live controls fail closed; existing profile, schedule and broadcast editors remain available.

sections.title: After a slow or failed action

blocks.text: Reload and inspect the current song number or queue state before trying a new action. A retried pending website action keeps its identity to prevent double advances. Selecting the already current song preserves its timestamp.

articles.title: Link your IRC account to your DJ login
articles.summary: Use a private one-time code to connect a verified IRC services account on each network.
articles.keywords: link services account tag nickserv sasl nickname network identity code expiry permission verified

items: Sign in to the website and open Live / IRC.
Generate a linking code under Your IRC accounts.
Sign in to IRC services on the network where Carrier is connected.
Send !link CODE privately to Carrier. Do not post the code in a channel.
Refresh Live / IRC to check the linked account/network.

blocks.text: /msg carrier !link YOUR_ONE_TIME_CODE

sections.title: Why nickname matching is not enough

blocks.text: New playlist and announcement controls use verified IRC services accounts. Changing your nickname keeps the link. Links are scoped to the IRC network; link separately on another network. Your account must still be the verified live DJ or an authorized administrator. Existing explicit bot account mappings may also grant access.

A code lasts five minutes and can be used once. If you exposed it publicly or it expired, generate a new one. Disconnect unwanted links from the same page; administrators can revoke links for other users.

articles.title: Advance songs and choose tracking mode
articles.summary: Timestamp actual prepared playback without losing the metadata Carrier captures independently.
articles.keywords: !track !next start next song jump number metadata prepared captured timestamps positions replay

items: With an attached prepared playlist, use Start next song in Live / IRC or !track next when song one begins.
Repeat when each following song begins.
To jump, select a song number on the website or use !track N. Skipped songs are not marked played.
Use !track without arguments to check the current position.

blocks.text:
!track
!track next
!track 5
!next always means the next scheduled show; it does not advance a song.

Selecting the already current song preserves its start time. A retried website advance does not run twice. To deliberately replay the same song, advance to a different number and then select it again.

Prepared mode publishes confirmed songs from your prepared list. Metadata mode uses the stream’s captured artist/title information. Carrier captures raw metadata in both modes, preserving both histories. An empty preparation uses metadata mode.

Switching to metadata ends the current prepared play at that time. Switching back retains history; select or advance a song to start its next timestamp. Selecting the already active tracking mode leaves playback intact.

If Carrier says no prepared playlist is active, check that exactly one preparation matched your live identity/window. You can still broadcast normally using metadata capture. Correct missing track information later in Sets / broadcasts.

items.label: Fix a track list after the show

articles.title: Turn automatic song announcements on or off
articles.summary: Keep IRC song messages quiet by default, or enable them for one broadcast from the website or bot.
articles.keywords: !songs announce announcements automatic quiet silent bot song notification off default on

blocks.text: Automatic song announcements are off for each new show unless you explicitly enable them in its preparation. In Live / IRC, use Enable song announcements or Disable song announcements. From your verified IRC account, use the commands below.

!songs on
!songs off
!songs status

The setting belongs to the current broadcast and survives a bot restart in that broadcast. It does not follow you into the next show. A copied preparation starts with the option unchecked. Website and IRC update the same setting; refresh the website to see an IRC change.

In metadata mode, a newly captured song produces Now playing. In prepared mode, advancing an actual song produces Track N/total. Enabling mid-show waits for the next song change. Duplicate polls, repeated current-song selections and retried website actions do not repeat messages.

Turning this off does not stop metadata capture, playback timestamps, archive updates or manual !np / !track replies. Existing show, station and listener-event announcements remain separate. Invited IRC channels also have their own station-announcement subscription.

articles.title: Requests, questions, goals and polls
articles.summary: Open the interaction you want and resolve private queues during your live show.
articles.keywords: requests questions !requests !qanswer !qskip !played !reject !goal !poll queue dedicate listener

blocks.text: Open requests in Live / IRC or use !requests on. Listeners can then submit requests. Review the queue and mark an item played or rejected; those controls update the queue and do not start audio or advance the prepared playlist.

!requests on
!requests list
!played 3
!reject 4
!requests off
Listeners can ask through IRC or the live activity page. The live DJ can view queued questions, answer one on air, or skip it. Unanswered questions and request queues remain private.

!questions
!qanswer 2
!qskip 3
Answering through Carrier announces the question; your answer is what you say on the stream.
Set an optional listener-count goal and text, or clear it. The bot reports when the target is reached.

!goal 10 tonight we try the mystery record
!goal clear
Create a question with at least two options separated by |. Listeners use !vote N or the website voting form. Votes can change until the poll closes.

!poll start next mood? | ambient | loud | strange
!poll
!poll stop

articles.title: Finish your show or hand off to another DJ
articles.summary: Tell Carrier who is next, disconnect cleanly and review the finished set.
articles.keywords: handoff relay next DJ autodj end stop stream disconnect final set

blocks.text: Name the expected DJ in Live / IRC or use !handoff nextdj before disconnecting. Carrier can recognize that DJ after a short AutoDJ gap. This records the expectation; it does not book their airtime or connect their broadcaster.
!handoff nextdj

items: Coordinate timing with the next DJ when someone is following.
Disconnect your live broadcaster so the next DJ or normal station automation can take over.
Allow Carrier to close/export the set, then open Sets / broadcasts.
Correct missing titles or track metadata and review an available recording if wanted.

articles.title: Add, edit, hide or restore a broadcast listing
articles.summary: Correct a missing or incomplete archive entry while retaining the original captured data.
articles.keywords: set broadcast session CRUD add edit remove delete hide restore missing title track metadata JSON archive

items: Open Sets / broadcasts from the DJ booth.
Choose the set and edit its episode/show details, public DJ name, UTC times or recording link.
Save and check the public archive listing.

blocks.text: The track editor contains JSON. Leave Replace the track list unchecked to let captured playback continue updating. Check it only when you intend to publish your corrected list; it becomes a listing override rather than a new stream capture.
Retain existing timestamps and durations if you want them preserved in your corrected list. Replacing with an empty list intentionally publishes no tracks.

Choose Add a set, enter its owning profile, UTC times, status and metadata, and save. Ordinary DJs can create listings for their own assigned profile; administrators can choose an owner. A planned listing does not create an AzuraCast booking or a Carrier preparation.

The delete confirmation hides the listing from the website and public API. Carrier’s captured data and audio are retained. An administrator can restore a hidden listing. Deleting a listing does not delete its DJ account or schedule.

sections.title: If a save reports a stale form

blocks.text: Reload the listing and review the latest captured information before saving again. The editor checks both listing version and source data to avoid silently overwriting a newer edit.

articles.title: Review recordings and publish an episode
articles.summary: Approve an available audio recording or attach a recording URL to your broadcast listing.
articles.keywords: recording audio download approve reject podcast rss feed discovery private published mp3

blocks.text: Open Recordings from the DJ booth. When recording discovery is enabled and a completed broadcast has available audio, a candidate may appear for its verified owner. Review it and approve or reject the candidate using the page controls.

Approval attaches that version of the recording to the listing. Public listening/download/feed access also requires a visible published listing and a valid approved recording. Discovery/download can be disabled by the station; every set is not guaranteed to have a recording. Unapproved private audio does not become public merely because a set exists.
Edit your broadcast listing and enter its recording/audio URL. Use a URL you are permitted to publish. Keep the recorded show title and times accurate.
Published completed episodes with suitable recording information are available through the station’s podcast endpoint. Hidden listings and unapproved private recordings stay out of the feed.

articles.title: Carrier: start with what you want to do
articles.summary: A guide to the station bot, its listener features and its connection to your website DJ booth.
articles.keywords: carrier bot guide commands IRC stream set track live website

blocks.text: AzuraCast supplies the live stream state. Your profile supplies recurring show details. The website supplies verified assignments and optional preparations. Carrier tracks numbered sets and interaction, then exports the archive. You connect/disconnect your broadcaster normally; there is no bot command to start the audio stream.

!np
!next
!listeners
!dj
!schedule
!next is the next scheduled DJ, not the next prepared song.
!tunein [tilde] checks you into the live show’s voluntary roll call. !tuneout removes your check-in. !couch and !tildes show the room.
Give props, ask a question, react, request a song when requests are open, or vote. Use IRC or the website live activity page where offered.
Use Live / IRC for episode details, prepared-song timestamps, song announcements, listener queues, goals and polls. Link a verified IRC services account for DJ controls.
Carrier exports captured sets to the website. You can correct the listing or track metadata and approve available audio after the show.
When the station has configured Mastodon, the live DJ can send one note for the set. Station automatic posts are configured separately.
!handoff nextdj names the expected replacement. It does not connect or schedule that DJ.
Polls, challenges, bingo, tilde battles and The Button are optional parts of live interaction.
!setcmd name response creates a command for one live set. !delcmd name removes it. Built-in commands cannot be replaced.

!last
!set 184
!djstats deepend
!stationstats
!records
!achievements
Invite it on a connected network. Channel announcement subscriptions are separate from the live DJ’s song-message preference.

sections.title: A show from start to finish

blocks.text: Book airtime, optionally prepare the episode, connect at your slot, confirm planned playback if used, disconnect cleanly, then review the listing.

articles.title: Listen and take part
articles.summary: Find the player, IRC commands, questions, requests, reactions and polls.
articles.keywords: listen couch tunein props ask react request dedicate vote public live interaction

blocks.text: Use the website player or a stream URL from !listen. Browse the schedule for airtime, DJs for profiles and the archive for past broadcasts. Use the upcoming page for published episode previews.

rows: Join or leave the live show’s voluntary couch roll call
See the room and represented communities
Queue a question for the DJ
React or inspect the room’s reaction summary
Request a song when the DJ has requests open
Submit a dedication when requests are open
See an open poll or vote for an option

blocks.text: The live activity page offers questions, open requests, reactions and poll voting while Carrier is available. It does not require a DJ login. Queued questions/requests are not a public message board; the DJ chooses which to answer or play.

Commands and submissions have cooldowns or limits. If a request is closed or you receive a wait message, respect it. A DJ deciding to close requests or disable song announcements is a show preference.

articles.title: Invite Carrier and choose channel announcements
articles.summary: Use commands in another IRC channel while controlling whether it receives station event messages.
articles.keywords: invite channel announce subscription operator owner part carrier announcements on off

blocks.text: If invites are enabled, invite Carrier normally. Invited channels are remembered across restarts. Use the bot’s actual nickname if it differs on that network.
/invite carrier #yourchannel

rows: Subscribe this invited channel to station announcements
Keep commands available while disabling station announcements
Remove Carrier and forget the invited channel

blocks.text: The inviter, a channel operator or a bot administrator can manage these settings, subject to the existing bot configuration.

!carrier announce controls whether the invited channel receives station messages. !songs controls whether the live broadcast produces automatic new-song messages. Enabling one does not force the other on. Direct command replies such as !np still answer the requesting channel.

articles.title: Games and temporary show commands
articles.summary: Use optional challenges, bingo, tilde battles, The Button or a command that lasts for one set.
articles.keywords: challenge answer random results bingo battle button temporary setcmd delcmd fun

blocks.text:
!challenge name a song you secretly love
!answer your answer
!challenge results
!challenge random
!challenge stop
The DJ starts/manages the challenge; listeners submit answers.
!bingo privately gives a listener a randomized 3×3 card for the live set. Some squares are marked automatically. The live DJ’s !bingo mark control handles manual marks.

!bingo
!bingo marks
!bingo marks lists valid mark keys. The live DJ can use !bingo mark KEY for an event that has just happened.

!battle start tilde.club | ctrl-c.club
!battle
!battle stop
Listeners identify a community with !tunein your.tilde. The live DJ controls starting/stopping the battle.
!button is optional room activity with a cooldown. !fun lists the room’s extra commands.

!setcmd lore https://example.com/show-lore
!lore
!delcmd lore
The live DJ can add a simple response for one set. Existing Carrier commands are reserved. The command ends with the set.

articles.title: Send an optional Mastodon note
articles.summary: Use the one-per-set DJ note when the station has enabled its Mastodon integration.
articles.keywords: mastodon federation transmission post note announcement social cooldown

sections.title: One DJ note for the set

blocks.text: During your live set, enter the Mastodon note in Live / IRC or use !show mastodon with the text. The station must have configured posting; an unavailable integration does not become available merely because the form is present.
!show mastodon tonight is mostly weird synths

Automatic live/show/record posts use the bot’s station configuration, eligibility rules and cooldowns. Your song-announcement preference controls IRC song messages, not Mastodon. Avoid repeating a failed action until you have checked its result.

articles.title: Activate DJs and assign their stations
articles.summary: Use verified username pickers, link profiles and manage website roles without changing streaming accounts.
articles.keywords: admin administrator activation DJ accounts streamer id username picker station mapping roles profile disabled delete restore

sections.title: Add or activate a website DJ

items: Open Administration → DJs and choose the account editor.
Choose the authentication station and select the AzuraCast DJ username from the directory. You normally do not need to look up a streamer ID manually.
Enable website login, choose the website role and link the public DJ profile.
Choose each station assignment and the corresponding DJ username in that station.
Save. The selected upstream account is verified again.

blocks.text: The identity is a station/streamer pair, not a display name. A DJ may use different streamer accounts in different stations. The username directory makes selection easier; manual IDs remain a fallback when lookup is unavailable. Keep existing assignments unless you intend to change them.

A website administrator can manage other DJs, profiles, schedules and listings. Protected administrator access comes from private server configuration and cannot be removed through the ordinary account form. New assignments do not grant access to the server or Docker.

Disabling prevents website editing/login. Deleting the website DJ removes website access and station assignments while retaining the AzuraCast streaming account, public profile and captured broadcasts. Manage those separately if needed. Deleted website accounts can be restored through the DJ list.
Use Activity to inspect website changes. Carrier integration also shows synchronization/health and recent integration events.

articles.title: Check Carrier and recording availability
articles.summary: Understand synchronization, verified live identity and optional services before troubleshooting an editor.
articles.keywords: health offline carrier sync verification broadcasts recordings discovery schedule API directory timeout fail closed

blocks.text: Administration → Carrier integration shows health, synchronization and recent actions. Check that account assignments are current and the radio data is recent. Website live writes synchronize first; periodic synchronization keeps the permission snapshot fresh.

Carrier controls require a recent permission snapshot and current live identity. An offline bot, stale sync or unavailable upstream verification prevents live writes. Profile, schedule and broadcast editing use their existing services and remain available when their own checks succeed.

Discovery requires an ended broadcast with a verified identity and available AzuraCast recording. The administrator controls discovery/download configuration. DJ approval and listing visibility govern publication. A missing candidate does not mean the listing or captured track data has been deleted.

Use the repository’s versioned deployment guides for installation, private keys, Unix socket permissions, source updates and code rollback. DJs should not need those details to operate a show. Server credentials and configuration are never included in this public Help catalog.

articles.title: Something is not working
articles.summary: Check the right layer for login, streaming, schedule, playlist, live-control or recording problems.
articles.keywords: error help troubleshoot failure offline unavailable 403 conflict stale expired no sound cannot connect

sections.title: Login works for streaming, but not the website

blocks.text: Ask an administrator to check website activation, profile link and station assignments. The streaming account and website role are separate. A password error still refers to your DJ streaming credentials.

sections.title: Broadcaster cannot connect or audio is silent

blocks.text: Recheck the supplied host, DJ port, mount, Icecast mode and personal DJ credentials. Test your input routing and levels. Include the exact broadcaster error when asking for help; never include the password.

A slot may overlap another DJ, its current version may have changed, or the upstream schedule could not be confirmed. Reload before retrying, inspect the station timezone and choose an available time. Do not treat a failed save as a booking.

Confirm your broadcaster is on the main assigned station and the public site reports a live DJ. Wait for a poll/synchronization cycle, then reload Live / IRC. Ask the administrator to check the actual station/streamer assignment and Carrier status. A matching displayed DJ name alone does not prove permission.

Check its station, enabled state, owner and UTC window. Exactly one preparation must match. If it was already used or several match, Carrier uses ordinary metadata capture. Continue the show and correct the archive later if needed.

sections.title: IRC says I am not the live DJ

blocks.text: Sign in to IRC services and link that account on that network. A nickname is not sufficient for new playlist/announcement controls. Check that your website assignment matches the actual live streamer.

sections.title: Song announcements are on, but no message appears

blocks.text: In prepared mode, advance the song when it starts. In metadata mode, send a genuinely new artist/title. Enabling mid-song does not announce it retroactively. An invited channel must also subscribe to station announcements. !songs does not mute other station event messages.

The broadcast may still be live, recording may be disabled, no upstream recording may exist, or discovery may not have verified that broadcast. Ask the administrator to check availability. You can attach an existing permitted recording URL through your listing editor.

Reload and inspect the result before choosing another action. Retried action IDs protect live writes, but another newly generated Next action is a separate advance. A stale form needs a reload, not a forced resubmission.

sections.title: Ask for help with useful details

items: Your software and operating system.
Which website page or command you used.
The exact error and approximate time.
Your DJ username, station name and affected set number if relevant.
No passwords, private keys or linking codes.

articles.title: Contribute audio or a special event
articles.summary: Make a station ID, jingle, one-off show, takeover or relay without needing Git knowledge.
articles.keywords: community contribute station ID jingle audio license event takeover relay submissions git

blocks.text: Bring a short station ID or jingle to #tilderadio. Include its title, creator credit and the license/permission you want attached. The contribution page shows the station’s current preferred formats and duration guidance.
Include the concept, rough length, possible dates/times, participants and whether it needs a live slot or several handoffs. Agree the plan with the station before publishing it.
Experienced contributors can use the existing audio and metadata files described in the contribution guide. Everyone else can bring the idea/file to IRC and arrange a suitable submission.

articles.title: Advanced: edit profile JSON in Git
articles.summary: Keep the existing file-based contribution workflow available alongside the website editor.
articles.keywords: git JSON profile sample validation formats file slug

blocks.text:
git clone https://github.com/TildeRadio/site.git
cd site
cp data/djs/example.json.sample data/djs/your-nick.json
$EDITOR data/djs/your-nick.json
php bin/validate-djs.php
Use lowercase letters, numbers and hyphens for the profile filename/slug. Never add credentials. Run the validator and keep changes scoped to your profile and intended avatar files.
The repository README documents optional biography, avatar, links, recurring show, timezone, formats and favorites. The website editor is normally easier for DJs.

blocks.text: No station API key is required for these public feeds. They do not expose unplayed private playlists, private listener queues or unpublished recordings. Website listing corrections/visibility affect the public archive. Private authentication, schedule management and Carrier control are separate authenticated services.

blocks.text: Examples use the default ! prefix. A network may use a different configured prefix. Some controls require a live set, a verified services account or an administrator. Existing DJ grants may also authorize older show controls; link your account for the new playlist/song controls. Commands have cooldowns and may reply privately.
